p.src: Now Cao Cao said to He Jin that day, “The scourge of the eunuchs has existed in every age; but rulers should never have granted them such power and favor as to let matters come to this pass. If you wish to punish the guilty, remove only the chief culprits and hand them over to a single jailer. Why summon troops from every quarter? If you seek to kill them all, the plan will inevitably become known. I predict that it will surely fail.” He Jin said angrily, “Do you too harbor selfish motives, Mengde?” Cao Cao withdrew, saying, “The man who brings disorder to the realm will surely be He Jin.” He Jin then secretly dispatched envoys bearing confidential edicts, and they rode through the night to the various garrisons.

p.src: Now Dong Zhuo, General of the Vanguard, Marquis of Lixiang, and Inspector of Xiliang, had earlier failed to distinguish himself against the Yellow Turbans. The court intended to punish him, but he escaped by bribing the Ten Regular Attendants; later he cultivated powerful courtiers and thus gained high office. Commanding two hundred thousand troops in the western provinces, he constantly harbored thoughts of rebellion. When the edict arrived, he was overjoyed, mustered his soldiers and horses, and set them marching in successive columns; he ordered his son-in-law, General of the Household Niu Fu, to hold Shaanxi, while he himself led Li Jue, Guo Si, Zhang Ji, Fan Chou, and the army toward Luoyang. p.src: He Jin received the memorial and showed it to the ministers. Zheng Tai, Attendant Censor, remonstrated: “Dong Zhuo is a jackal and a wolf. If he is admitted into the capital, he will surely devour men.” He Jin said, “You are too suspicious and unfit to plan great affairs.” Lu Zhi also remonstrated: “I have long known Dong Zhuo’s character. His face is benign, but his heart is cruel; once he enters the imperial precincts, calamity is certain to arise. It would be better to stop him from coming and thereby avert disorder.” He Jin would not listen, so Zheng Tai and Lu Zhi both resigned their offices and departed. More than half the ministers of the court left. He Jin sent men to welcome Dong Zhuo at Mianchi, but Dong Zhuo held his army stationary.

p.src: When Zhang Rang and the others learned that outside troops had arrived, they conferred together: “This is He Jin’s scheme; unless we strike first, every one of our clans will be exterminated.” They first concealed fifty armed executioners inside Jiade Gate of Changle Palace, then went in and told Empress Dowager He, “The General-in-Chief has forged an edict and summoned outside troops to the capital, intending to destroy us. We beg Your Majesty to take pity and save us.” The Empress Dowager said, “You may go to the General-in-Chief’s residence and beg forgiveness.” Zhang Rang said, “If we go to his residence, our flesh and bones will be ground to dust. We beg Your Majesty to summon the General-in-Chief into the palace and command him to desist. If he refuses, we shall merely ask to die before Your Majesty.” The Empress Dowager therefore issued an edict summoning He Jin. On receiving the edict, He Jin prepared to go at once. His secretary Chen Lin remonstrated: “This edict from the Empress Dowager must be a plot of the Ten Regular Attendants. You must on no account go. If you go, calamity will surely befall you.” He Jin said, “The Empress Dowager summons me. What calamity could there be?” Yuan Shao said, “Our plan is already leaked and the whole affair exposed. Do you still intend to enter the palace, General?” Cao Cao said, “First summon the Ten Regular Attendants outside; only then may you enter.” He Jin laughed. “That is a child’s counsel. I hold the authority of the whole realm. What could the Ten Regular Attendants dare do to me?” Yuan Shao said, “If you are determined to go, we shall lead armored men as your escort against the unexpected.” Thereupon Yuan Shao and Cao Cao each selected five hundred elite soldiers and placed them under Yuan Shao’s younger brother Yuan Shu. Yuan Shu donned full armor and arrayed the troops outside Qingsuo Gate. Yuan Shao and Cao Cao, wearing swords, escorted He Jin to the front of Changle Palace. A palace eunuch conveyed the sovereign command: “The Empress Dowager has summoned the General-in-Chief alone. No one else may enter without permission.” Yuan Shao, Cao Cao, and all the others were stopped outside the palace gate. He Jin strode proudly inside alone. When he reached the gate of Jiade Hall, Zhang Rang and Duan Gui came out to meet him, and their men surrounded him. He Jin was greatly alarmed. Zhang Rang sternly accused him: “What crime had Empress Dowager Dong committed that you recklessly poisoned her to death? And when the Mother of the Realm was buried, you feigned illness and did not attend! You were merely a petty butcher and wine seller. We recommended you to the Emperor and brought you wealth and honor; yet instead of repaying us, you seek to murder us! You call us utterly corrupt—but who, then, are the pure?” In panic, He Jin sought a way out, but every palace gate was shut. The ambushed soldiers rushed forth together and hacked him in two. p.src: After Zhang Rang and the others had killed He Jin, Yuan Shao waited long but did not see him emerge, so he shouted outside the palace gate, “General, please mount your carriage!” Zhang Rang and the others threw He Jin’s head over the wall and proclaimed, “He Jin plotted rebellion and has now been executed. All others who were coerced into following him are hereby pardoned.” Yuan Shao cried out fiercely, “The castrated officials have murdered a great minister! Let all who would destroy these wicked traitors come and join the fight!” He Jin’s officer Wu Kuang immediately set fire outside Qingsuo Gate. Yuan Shu led his troops in a charge into the palace precincts. Whenever they saw a eunuch, high or low, they killed him without distinction. Yuan Shao and Cao Cao broke through the gates and entered. Zhao Zhong, Cheng Kuang, Xia Yun, and Guo Sheng were chased before Cuihua Tower and hacked to pulp. Flames from the palace soared into the sky. Zhang Rang, Duan Gui, Cao Jie, and Hou Lan abducted the Empress Dowager, the Crown Prince, and the Prince of Chenliu into the inner apartments, then took a rear passage toward the Northern Palace. At that time Lu Zhi, though he had resigned his office, had not yet departed. Seeing the upheaval in the palace, he donned armor, took up a halberd, and stood beneath the gallery. From afar he saw Duan Gui forcing Empress Dowager He along and shouted, “Duan Gui, you rebel! How dare you abduct the Empress Dowager?” Duan Gui turned and fled. The Empress Dowager leapt out through a window, and Lu Zhi hastened to rescue her, bringing her to safety. Wu Kuang fought his way into the inner court and saw He Miao coming out with sword in hand. Wu Kuang shouted, “He Miao conspired in the murder of his own brother. Let us all kill him!” The others all cried, “We will slay the villain who plotted against his brother!” He Miao tried to flee, but they surrounded him on every side and hacked him to pieces. Yuan Shao then ordered the soldiers to split up and kill the families of the Ten Regular Attendants. Old and young alike were utterly exterminated, and many beardless men were mistakenly killed. Meanwhile Cao Cao had the palace fires extinguished, asked Empress Dowager He to assume temporary charge of affairs, and sent troops in pursuit of Zhang Rang and his fellows to search for the Young Emperor.

p.src: Meanwhile, Zhang Rang and Duan Gui abducted the Young Emperor and the Prince of Chenliu, then fled through smoke and flames, running all night until they reached Mount Beimang. Around the third watch, loud shouts arose behind them as pursuing troops and horses drew near. At their head was Min Gong, an assistant officer of Henan, who cried aloud, “Rebels, halt!” Seeing that the situation was desperate, Zhang Rang threw himself into the river and died. Unable to tell friend from foe, the Emperor and the Prince of Chenliu dared not make a sound and hid among the tangled grass beside the river. The troops scattered in pursuit, unaware of the Emperor’s whereabouts. The Emperor and the prince lay hidden until the fourth watch; dew began to fall, and faint with hunger, they embraced and wept. Fearing discovery, they stifled their sobs amid the wild grass. The Prince of Chenliu said, “We cannot linger here. We must seek another way to survive.” The two then tied their garments together and clambered up the riverbank. Thorns covered the ground, and in the darkness no path could be seen. Just when they were at a loss, hundreds upon hundreds of fireflies suddenly gathered, their glow illuminating the darkness as they circled only before the Emperor. The Prince of Chenliu said, “Heaven is aiding us brothers!” They followed the fireflies and gradually found a path. By the fifth watch, their feet hurt so badly that they could go no farther. They saw a haystack beside a hillock, and the Emperor and the prince lay down next to it. In front of the haystack stood a country manor. That night, the master of the manor dreamed that two red suns fell behind his estate. Startled awake, he threw on his clothes, went outside, and looked all around. Seeing a red radiance soar into the sky above the haystack behind the manor, he hurried over and found two people lying beside it. The master asked, “Whose sons are you two young men?” The Emperor dared not answer. Pointing to the Emperor, the Prince of Chenliu said, “This is the reigning Emperor. He fled here for refuge after the uprising of the Ten Regular Attendants. I am the Emperor’s younger brother, the Prince of Chenliu.” Greatly startled, the master bowed twice and said, “Your servant is Cui Yi, younger brother of Cui Lie, who served the late emperor as Minister over the Masses. Because I saw the Ten Regular Attendants selling offices and persecuting the worthy, I withdrew to live here in seclusion.” He helped the Emperor into the manor, then knelt and presented him with food and wine.

p.src: Meanwhile, Min Gong caught up with Duan Gui and seized him, demanding to know where the Son of Heaven was. Duan Gui said that they had become separated on the road and that he did not know where the Emperor had gone. Min Gong killed Duan Gui, hung his head beneath his horse’s neck, and divided his troops to search in every direction. He himself rode on alone, searching along the road. By chance he came to Cui Yi’s manor. Seeing the severed head, Cui Yi questioned him, and Min Gong related everything in detail. Cui Yi led Min Gong to the Emperor, and sovereign and subject wept bitterly together. Min Gong said, “The realm cannot be without its sovereign for even one day. I beg Your Majesty to return to the capital.” There was only one lean horse at Cui Yi’s manor, and it was prepared for the Emperor to ride. Min Gong and the Prince of Chenliu shared another horse. Less than three li after leaving the manor, they met Minister over the Masses Wang Yun, Grand Commandant Yang Biao, Colonel of the Left Army Chunyu Qiong, Colonel of the Right Army Zhao Meng, Colonel of the Rear Army Bao Xin, Colonel of the Central Army Yuan Shao, and a company of several hundred men and horses who had come to meet the imperial party; sovereign and subjects all wept. They first sent a man to carry Duan Gui’s head to the capital and display it publicly as a warning. They provided fine horses for the Emperor and the Prince of Chenliu, then escorted the Emperor back to the capital. Earlier, the children of Luoyang had sung: “Emperor no emperor, prince no prince; a thousand carriages and ten thousand riders flee to Beimang.” Now the prophecy had indeed come true.

p.src: The imperial party had gone only a few li when they suddenly saw banners blotting out the sun and dust veiling the sky as a force of soldiers and horses approached. The officials turned pale, and the Emperor too was greatly alarmed. Yuan Shao spurred his horse forward and demanded who they were. From amid the embroidered banners, a general galloped forth and demanded sternly, “Where is the Son of Heaven?” The Emperor trembled and could not speak. The Prince of Chenliu reined his horse forward and rebuked him: “Who are you?” Dong Zhuo replied, “I am Dong Zhuo, Inspector of Xiliang.” The Prince of Chenliu said, “Have you come to protect His Majesty? Or have you come to abduct him?” Dong Zhuo answered, “I have come expressly to protect His Majesty.” The Prince of Chenliu said, “If you have come to protect him, the Son of Heaven is here. Why do you not dismount?” Greatly startled, Dong Zhuo hurriedly dismounted and bowed beside the road. The Prince of Chenliu spoke soothingly to Dong Zhuo and, from beginning to end, never once misspoke. Dong Zhuo secretly marveled at him, and already conceived the idea of deposing one emperor and enthroning another. That day they returned to the palace and met Empress Dowager He, whereupon they all wept bitterly. When the palace was inspected, the Imperial Seal of State was found to be missing. Dong Zhuo stationed his army outside the city and entered it every day with armored cavalry, swaggering through the streets and leaving the people fearful and uneasy. Dong Zhuo came and went within the imperial palace without the slightest restraint. Bao Xin, Colonel of the Rear Army, went to see Yuan Shao and said that Dong Zhuo surely harbored treacherous designs and must be eliminated at once. Yuan Shao said, “The court has only just been restored to order. We must not act rashly.” Bao Xin then met Wang Yun and told him the same thing. Wang Yun said, “Allow us time to discuss it.” Bao Xin then led the troops under his command away to Mount Tai.

p.src: Dong Zhuo enticed the soldiers formerly under He Jin and his brother to join him, bringing them all under his control. In private he asked Li Ru, “I wish to depose the Emperor and enthrone the Prince of Chenliu. What do you think?” Li Ru said, “The court now lacks a true master. If you do not act at this moment, delay will bring unforeseen change. Tomorrow, assemble all the officials in Wenming Garden and proclaim to them the deposition and enthronement. Behead anyone who refuses, and your authority will be established this very day.” Dong Zhuo was delighted. The next day he laid out a grand banquet and invited every high minister and noble. All the high officials feared Dong Zhuo; who dared not attend? Only after all the officials had arrived did Dong Zhuo slowly approach the garden gate, dismount, and enter the banquet wearing his sword. After several rounds of wine, Dong Zhuo ordered the drinking and music stopped, then declared sternly, “I have something to say. Let every officer listen in silence.” Every official listened intently. Dong Zhuo said, “The Son of Heaven is lord of all the people. Without majesty and dignity, he cannot serve the ancestral temples or preserve the altars of the land and grain. The present Emperor is weak and timid, unlike the Prince of Chenliu, who is intelligent and fond of learning and can inherit the great throne. I wish to depose the Emperor and enthrone the Prince of Chenliu. What do you ministers think?” Having heard him out, the officials dared not utter a sound. One man at the banquet shoved aside his table, strode out, stood before the feast, and shouted, “No! No! Who are you to dare utter such outrageous words? The Son of Heaven is the legitimate son of the late emperor and has committed no fault whatsoever. How can you recklessly discuss deposing him and enthroning another? Do you mean to become a usurping traitor?” Dong Zhuo looked and saw that it was Ding Yuan, Inspector of Jingzhou. Dong Zhuo angrily shouted, “Those who obey me live; those who oppose me die!” He drew his sword and made to behead Ding Yuan. At that moment, Li Ru saw a man behind Ding Yuan, imposing in bearing and awe-inspiring in might, gripping a halberd with a painted shaft and glaring furiously. Li Ru hurried forward and said, “This is a banquet; affairs of state should not be discussed here today. It will not be too late to debate the matter publicly in the council hall tomorrow.” Everyone urged Ding Yuan to mount his horse and leave.

I wish to depose the Emperor and enthrone the Prince of Chenliu. What do you ministers think?”
Having heard him out, the officials dared not utter a sound.
One man at the banquet shoved aside his table, strode out, stood before the feast, and shouted, “No!
No!
Who are you to dare utter such outrageous words?
The Son of Heaven is the legitimate son of the late emperor and has committed no fault whatsoever. How can you recklessly discuss deposing him and enthroning another?
Do you mean to become a usurping traitor?”
Dong Zhuo looked and saw that it was Ding Yuan, Inspector of Jingzhou.
Dong Zhuo angrily shouted, “Those who obey me live; those who oppose me die!”
He drew his sword and made to behead Ding Yuan.
At that moment, Li Ru saw a man behind Ding Yuan, imposing in bearing and awe-inspiring in might, gripping a halberd with a painted shaft and glaring furiously.
Li Ru hurried forward and said, “This is a banquet; affairs of state should not be discussed here today.
It will not be too late to debate the matter publicly in the council hall tomorrow.”
Everyone urged Ding Yuan to mount his horse and leave.

p.src: Dong Zhuo asked the officials, “Is what I have said in accord with justice?” Lu Zhi said, “Your Excellency is mistaken. In ancient times, when Tai Jia proved unenlightened, Yi Yin banished him to the Tong Palace. The Prince of Changyi had been on the throne only twenty-seven days when he committed more than three thousand offenses, and so Huo Guang reported to the imperial ancestral temple and deposed him. Though the present Emperor is young, he is intelligent, benevolent, and wise, and has committed not the slightest fault. You are merely an inspector from an outlying commandery, have never taken part in governing the state, and possess neither the great talent of Yi Yin nor that of Huo Guang. How can you forcibly take charge of deposing and enthroning emperors? The sage said, ‘If one possesses Yi Yin’s purpose, it is permissible; without Yi Yin’s purpose, it is usurpation.’” Dong Zhuo flew into a rage, drew his sword, and stepped forward to kill Lu Zhi. Consultant Peng Bo remonstrated, “Master of Writing Lu is esteemed by all within the realm. If you harm him first, I fear the whole empire will be terrified.” Dong Zhuo then stopped. Minister over the Masses Wang Yun said, “The matter of deposition and enthronement should not be discussed after drinking. Let us deliberate again another day.” Thereupon all the officials dispersed.

p.src: Dong Zhuo stood at the garden gate with his hand upon his sword when he suddenly saw a man mounted on a galloping horse, halberd in hand, riding back and forth outside the gate. Dong Zhuo asked Li Ru, “Who is that man?” Li Ru replied, “That is Ding Yuan’s adopted son. His surname is Lü, his given name Bu, and his courtesy name Fengxian. My lord, you should avoid him for the present.” Dong Zhuo accordingly withdrew into the garden and concealed himself. The next day, word came that Ding Yuan had brought his army outside the city and was challenging them to battle. Enraged, Dong Zhuo led out his troops with Li Ru to meet him. When the two armies had drawn up opposite each other, Lü Bu appeared wearing a golden crown over his bound hair, a battle robe embroidered with a hundred flowers, Tangni armor, and a jeweled belt adorned with lions. Urging on his horse and leveling his halberd, he followed Ding Jianyang to the front of the lines. Jianyang pointed at Dong Zhuo and cursed him: “The realm has suffered the misfortune of eunuchs abusing their power, reducing the people to misery. You have not rendered the slightest service. How dare you recklessly speak of deposing one sovereign and enthroning another, and seek to throw the court into disorder?” Before Dong Zhuo could reply, Lü Bu spurred his horse and charged straight at him. Dong Zhuo fled in panic, and Jianyang led his army in a sweeping attack. Dong Zhuo’s forces suffered a crushing defeat. They retreated more than thirty li, made camp, and assembled to deliberate. Dong Zhuo said, “From what I have seen, Lü Bu is no ordinary man. If I could gain his service, what would I have to fear anywhere under Heaven?” A man stepped forward from before the command tent and said, “My lord, do not worry. Lü Bu and I come from the same district. I know that he is brave but witless, and that at the sight of profit he forgets all loyalty. May I use my persuasive tongue to induce Lü Bu to come and submit without a struggle?” Dong Zhuo was delighted. Looking at the speaker, he saw that it was Li Su, General of the Gentlemen of the Rapid-as-Tigers. Dong Zhuo asked, “How will you persuade him?” Li Su replied, “I have heard that my lord possesses a famous horse called Red Hare, which can cover a thousand li in a day. I must have that horse, together with gold and jewels, to bind his heart through gain. Then I shall press my arguments, and Lü Bu will surely turn against Ding Yuan and come over to my lord.” Dong Zhuo asked Li Ru, “Will this plan work?” Li Ru replied, “If my lord desires to possess all under Heaven, why begrudge a single horse?” Dong Zhuo gladly gave him the horse, and also a thousand taels of gold, dozens of lustrous pearls, and a jade belt.

p.src: Bearing the gifts, Li Su made his way to Lü Bu’s camp. The soldiers posted in ambush surrounded him. Li Su said, “Report at once to General Lü that an old friend has come to see him.” The soldiers carried the message, and Lü Bu ordered that he be admitted. On seeing Lü Bu, Li Su said, “My worthy younger brother, I trust you have been well since we parted!” Lü Bu bowed and said, “It has been a long time since we met. Where are you living now?” Li Su replied, “I now hold the office of General of the Gentlemen of the Rapid-as-Tigers. When I heard that my worthy brother was upholding the state, my joy knew no bounds. I have a fine horse that can travel a thousand li in a day, cross rivers, and climb mountains as though treading level ground. Its name is Red Hare. I have come expressly to present it to my worthy brother, that it may add to your tiger-like might.” Lü Bu at once ordered the horse brought over for him to inspect. p.src: When Lü Bu saw the horse, he was overjoyed and thanked Li Su, saying, “Elder brother, you have given me this magnificent steed. How can I ever repay you?” Li Su replied, “I came for friendship’s sake. How could I expect repayment?” Lü Bu laid out wine and entertained him. When they were merry with wine, Li Su said, “Though I have seldom been able to see my worthy younger brother, your honored father has often come to visit me.” Lü Bu said, “Elder brother, you are drunk! My late father has been dead for many years. How could he possibly have met you?” Li Su laughed heartily and said, “No, no. I meant Inspector Ding, your father of the present day.” Alarmed, Lü Bu said, “My service under Ding Jianyang is born of necessity.” Li Su said, “My worthy brother possesses talent enough to uphold the heavens and span the seas. Who within the Four Seas does not admire you? Fame, honor, wealth, and rank are as easily yours as an object taken from your own pouch. Why speak of necessity and remain beneath another man?” Lü Bu replied, “My only regret is that I have not met a worthy lord.” Li Su smiled and said, “‘A fine bird chooses the tree in which it roosts; a worthy minister chooses the lord whom he serves.’ If you fail to seize the opportunity early, regret will come too late.” Lü Bu asked, “Since you serve at court, whom do you consider the hero of our age?” Li Su replied, “I have surveyed all the ministers, and none can compare with Dong Zhuo. Dong Zhuo respects worthy men and treats scholars with courtesy; his rewards and punishments are clearly determined. In the end, he will accomplish a great enterprise.” Lü Bu said, “I wish to follow him, but regret that I have no means of gaining an introduction.” Li Su brought out the gold, pearls, and jade belt and arranged them before Lü Bu. Startled, Lü Bu asked, “Why have you brought these?” Li Su ordered the attendants away, then told Lü Bu, “Lord Dong has long admired your illustrious name and expressly commanded me to present these to you. Red Hare was likewise a gift from Lord Dong.” Lü Bu said, “Since Lord Dong holds me in such esteem, how can I repay him?” Li Su replied, “Even a man as untalented as I have been made General of the Gentlemen of the Rapid-as-Tigers; if you were to go to him, your future eminence would be beyond words.” Lü Bu said, “I regret that I have not even the smallest merit to offer as a gift upon my introduction.” Li Su said, “Such merit lies within a turn of your hand; it is only that you are unwilling to perform the deed.” Lü Bu pondered for a long while, then said, “What if I kill Ding Yuan and bring his army over to Dong Zhuo?” Li Su replied, “If my worthy brother can do that, it will truly be a service beyond compare! But the matter permits no delay; you must decide and act swiftly.” Lü Bu arranged with Li Su to come and surrender the following day, and Li Su took his leave.

p.src: That night, during the second watch, Lü Bu took up his sword and went straight into Ding Yuan’s tent. Ding Yuan was reading by candlelight. Seeing Lü Bu enter, he asked, “My son, what brings you here?” Lü Bu replied, “I am a man of proud and noble bearing! How could I consent to be your son?” Ding Yuan asked, “Fengxian, why has your heart changed?” Lü Bu stepped forward and struck off Ding Yuan’s head with a single blow. Then he cried aloud, “All of you, listen! Ding Yuan was without benevolence, and I have killed him. Those willing to follow me shall remain here; those unwilling may depart!” More than half the soldiers dispersed. The next day, Lü Bu carried Ding Yuan’s head to see Li Su. Li Su then conducted Lü Bu into Dong Zhuo’s presence. Dong Zhuo was overjoyed and laid out wine to entertain him. Dong Zhuo was the first to bow, saying, “Now that I have obtained the general, I am like parched seedlings receiving sweet rain.” Lü Bu invited Dong Zhuo to sit, then bowed to him and said, “If my lord does not disdain me, I beg leave to acknowledge you as my adoptive father.” Dong Zhuo bestowed golden armor and a brocade robe upon Lü Bu, and after drinking their fill, they dispersed. From then on, Dong Zhuo’s power and prestige grew still greater. He assumed the duties of General of the Van, enfeoffed his younger brother Dong Min as General of the Left and Marquis of Hu, and appointed Lü Bu Cavalry Commandant, General of the Household, and Marquis of Duting.

p.src: Li Ru urged Dong Zhuo to settle the plan for deposing and enthroning without delay. Dong Zhuo therefore held a banquet within the palace and summoned the highest ministers. He ordered Lü Bu to command more than a thousand armored soldiers as guards on either side. On that day, Grand Tutor Yuan Wei and all the officials attended. After several rounds of wine, Dong Zhuo drew his sword and declared, “The present sovereign is benighted and weak, and unfit to tend the ancestral temples. Following the precedents of Yi Yin and Huo Guang, I shall depose the emperor as Prince of Hongnong and enthrone the Prince of Chenliu as emperor. Anyone who refuses shall be beheaded!” The assembled ministers were terrified, and none dared answer. Then Yuan Shao, Colonel of the Central Army, stepped boldly forward and said, “The present sovereign has been on the throne only a short while and has committed no failure of virtue. You seek to depose the rightful heir and enthrone a son of a concubine. What is that, if not treason?” Dong Zhuo said furiously, “The affairs of the realm rest with me! If I do this today, who dares refuse me? Do you think my sword is not sharp?” Yuan Shao also drew his sword and said, “Your sword may be sharp, but mine has never been blunt!” The two confronted each other across the banquet table. Indeed:
